_doc: Star Trek — six decades of planets-of-the-week. Some are civilisations the Federation argued with for a season; several appeared once and were never mentioned again, which is exactly why they are worth listing.

destinations.name: Bajor
destinations.blurb: A deeply devout agrarian world rebuilding after fifty years of occupation, with terraced farms, monasteries full of Orbs, and a wormhole overhead the Bajorans call the Celestial Temple.

destinations.name: Cardassia Prime
destinations.blurb: A hot, dry world of brutalist architecture and enthusiastic surveillance, where trials conclude before they begin and the literature is genuinely magnificent. Dress warmly; they keep it at 30°C.

destinations.name: Trill
destinations.blurb: A temperate world of lakes and universities, and beneath it the Caves of Mak'ala, where the symbionts live in pools and a small committee decides who gets to carry several lifetimes of memory.

destinations.name: Betazed
destinations.blurb: A warm, gracious world of gardens, lakes and telepaths, where weddings are conducted entirely naked and nobody thinks that is odd. Privacy is a concept you will need to renegotiate.

destinations.name: Andoria
destinations.blurb: An ice moon whose cities are carved deep below the surface, home to a proud, quick-tempered, four-parent species who founded the Federation and remain slightly annoyed about the paperwork.

destinations.name: Nimbus III
destinations.blurb: A shared Federation-Klingon-Romulan colony founded to prove three empires could cooperate. Twenty years on it is a dust bowl with one bar, called Paradise City, ironically.

destinations.name: Talos IV
destinations.blurb: A blue-skied world of singing plants above and a city of enormous-brained illusionists below, who will show you anything you want and are the only planet under a Federation death penalty.

destinations.name: Sigma Iotia II
destinations.blurb: A world that found a book about 1920s Chicago gangsters and rebuilt its entire civilisation around it. Pinstripes, tommy guns, territorial bosses, and a cut going to the Federation.

destinations.name: Rura Penthe
destinations.blurb: The alien's graveyard: a frozen asteroid with a dilithium mine below and lethal cold above, so no guards are needed on the surface. There is a magnetic shield, and there is a way out.

destinations.name: Ba'ku
destinations.blurb: Six hundred people farming a valley inside a nebula, where metaphasic radiation from the rings stops anyone ageing. They gave up warp drive on purpose and seem entirely happy about it.

destinations.name: Argelius II
destinations.blurb: A hedonistic port world with a total prohibition on violence, famous for its cafés, dancers and complete lack of crime — a reputation that took a knock during a memorable series of murders.

destinations.name: Organia
destinations.blurb: An unremarkable pastoral village of placid peasants who have not changed in millennia, sitting on a strategically vital world. They are not peasants, and they will end your war for you.

destinations.name: Ceti Alpha V
destinations.blurb: Once habitable, until the neighbouring planet exploded and shifted its orbit. Now a sandstorm-scoured shell with one surviving lifeform, a burrowing eel, and some extremely aggrieved marooned colonists.

destinations.name: Boreth
destinations.blurb: A cold monastery world where Klingon clerics wait for Kahless to return, guard a set of time crystals, and will let you look into any future you like on the strict condition you then live it.

destinations.name: Wrigley's Pleasure Planet
destinations.blurb: Mentioned once, in passing, as the place crews go on leave and do not describe afterwards. The entire economy is diversion, and the brochures are considerably more discreet than the reviews.

destinations.name: Yonada
destinations.blurb: A generation ship disguised inside an asteroid, whose people believe their sky is the sky and that the Oracle punishing blasphemers is a god rather than a rather stern computer.

destinations.name: Freecloud
destinations.blurb: A lawless commercial world of holographic advertising that follows you down the street, where anything is for sale and the only real question is who is currently holding the debt.

destinations.name: Pahvo
destinations.blurb: An untouched forest world where every living thing vibrates in harmony and the whole planet hums one continuous chord. The inhabitants are the sound. They would like everyone to get along.
